title: A factorial that refuses to overflow

blocks.text: The course computes `n!` with a `do`-`while` loop that multiplies a `long` up. A `long` holds `20!` but not `21!`, and plain `*` would wrap around silently.

items: a negative `n` has no factorial: throw `IllegalArgumentException`;
when the result does not fit in a `long`, as for `of(21)`, throw `ArithmeticException` instead of returning a wrapped value. `Math.multiplyExact` does exactly that.

cases.says: of(21) throws ArithmeticException: 21! does not fit in a long.

concepts: A loop that multiplies a counter up can overflow, and the overflow must be detected rather than wrap.
